About Shahida
A neighbor.A professional.A public servant.
Shahida Merchant has spent her career in education, community service, and civic engagement. She is running for the Gavilan College Board of Trustees Area 3 because she believes every student in Gilroy deserves a college that works — and a board that listens.
Shahida Merchant
My Background
A career built on science, education, and service.
01
Scientist
Ashland Chemical
10 years as a scientist, applying rigorous analytical thinking to real-world challenges.
02
Chemistry & Physics Teacher
Salinas High School
23 years educating students in Chemistry and Physics, shaping the next generation of thinkers.
03
Adjunct Professor, Chemistry
Hartnell College, Salinas
Brought college-level chemistry instruction to students in the Salinas Valley.
04
STEM Lab Coordinator, Chemistry & Biology
Gavilan College
Retired from Gavilan College after serving students as a STEM Chemistry and Biology Lab Coordinator.
05
Master of Science, Organic Chemistry
Education
Graduate-level training in organic chemistry, forming the scientific foundation for decades of teaching and research.
Why I'm running
Gavilan College is one of the most important public institutions in our community. It opens doors for students who are the first in their families to attend college, for working adults who need new skills, and for neighbors who want to grow.
I am running because I believe the board should be a place of clear priorities, honest communication, and genuine accountability to the people it serves. I want to bring that kind of leadership to Area 3.
I will listen to students, faculty, staff, and community members. I will lead with transparency and purpose. And I will serve with the same commitment I have brought to every role in my life.
What I bring to the board
Education focus
A deep commitment to student success, equitable access, and learning environments that work for everyone.
Community roots
Decades of connection to Gilroy and the communities of Trustee Area 3 — I know this place and the people in it.
Accountable leadership
A track record of clear communication, responsible decision-making, and following through on commitments.
Community involvement
Rooted in Gilroy. Committed to service.
Second Vice President
Gilroy Lions International
Shahida serves as Second Vice President of the Gilroy Lions International, a nonprofit dedicated to serving the Gilroy community. Her work includes sight and vision programs, local charity and event volunteering, youth and education initiatives, student scholarships, and vision screening for local school students and migrant workers.

captures.title: Platform & Priorities | Shahida Merchant for Gavilan College Area 3
captures.text:
Campaign message|Share this site|Click here to look for your voting district|Volunteer sign-up
About ShahidaPlatformElection infoContact
Shahida Merchant · Gavilan College Board of Trustees Area 3
A platform built on listening, leading, and serving.
These are not talking points. They are commitments — grounded in the real needs of students, families, and the communities of Trustee Area 3.
01Student Success02Fiscal Accountability03Community Connection04Workforce & Economic Opportunity05Governance & Trust
01
Student Success
Every student deserves a clear path forward.
Gavilan College exists to help students succeed — from their first day to their last. That means removing barriers, strengthening support services, and making sure every student knows what they need to do to finish.
Specific commitments
Advocate for expanded counseling and advising so students get timely, accurate guidance on their academic path.
Support basic needs programs — food, housing, and childcare resources — that help students stay enrolled and focused.
Push for clear, transparent degree and transfer pathways so students can plan with confidence.
Ensure that career and technical education programs stay aligned with the real job market in our region.
02
Fiscal Accountability
Public money deserves public accountability.
The board is responsible for overseeing how Gavilan College spends public funds. That responsibility demands transparency, careful planning, and honest reporting — not just to auditors, but to the community.
Specific commitments
Review budget decisions with a clear focus on student outcomes — not administrative convenience.
Support open, accessible reporting so community members can understand how college resources are used.
Ask hard questions about long-term financial sustainability before approving major expenditures.
Ensure that bond and grant funds are spent as promised and tracked with full transparency.
03
Community Connection
Gavilan should reflect the community it serves.
Gilroy and the communities of Trustee Area 3 are diverse, working-class, and deeply invested in education. The board should reflect that — by listening actively, communicating clearly, and building real partnerships.
Specific commitments
Hold regular community listening sessions in Area 3 so residents can share their priorities directly.
Strengthen partnerships with Gilroy Unified School District to smooth the transition from high school to college.
Support outreach to first-generation college students and families who may not know what Gavilan offers.
Ensure that board meetings and communications are accessible — in language, format, and timing — to the full community.
04
Workforce & Economic Opportunity
A college that opens doors to real careers.
For many students in our community, Gavilan is the most direct route to a better job and a more stable life. The board should make sure the college is delivering on that promise.
Specific commitments
Support programs that connect students to internships, apprenticeships, and local employers.
Advocate for workforce programs that serve adults who are returning to school or changing careers.
Work with regional employers and economic development organizations to keep Gavilan's programs current and relevant.
Ensure that certificate and degree programs lead to living-wage jobs in our region.
05
Governance & Trust
A board that earns trust by doing its job well.
Good governance is not glamorous — but it matters. The board sets policy, hires the superintendent/president, and oversees the institution. Doing that well requires preparation, integrity, and a commitment to the public interest.
Specific commitments
Come prepared to every board meeting — having read the materials, asked questions in advance, and thought carefully about the decisions at hand.
Maintain clear boundaries between board oversight and day-to-day administration.
Support a board culture of respectful debate, honest disagreement, and shared accountability.
Report back to Area 3 constituents regularly — not just at election time.
I will listen. I will lead. I will serve.
These commitments are the foundation of my campaign. They will guide every vote I cast as a trustee. I am asking for your trust — and I intend to earn it.

the candidate's own platform, not an endorser's views, a navigation keyword, an opponent's
quote or a news mention. Preserve qualifications, conditions, dates and historical context.

quote from a successful captured page that mentions Israel, Palestine, Gaza or a related
issue. Explain platform attribution and identity; do not infer their politics.

pages/robots failures; explicitly bound the observation to those URLs, crawl limits and
capture dates. This is site silence within that scope, never political neutrality or proof
of no stance elsewhere. A blocked, empty, JavaScript-only or identity-uncertain site is
unavailable. no_website means no verified campaign URL in the inventory, not that none exists.
If a browser/PDF/other source is required, keep unavailable and explain the follow-up;
never paste invented source text into the cache. Source packets contain no search results.
